findings.title: Logout and missing-extra paths for the auth commands have no failure handling
findings.description:
`sq auth login`, `logout` and `status` each spawn the Codex runtime, but the failure table only covers the login wait and the `account()` call.
- **Logout:** D7 defines turn, login and account timeouts, but nothing bounds runtime start plus `AsyncCodex.logout()`. There is no row for a hung or failed logout, and no stated exit code or message. A logout that fails quietly leaves the user believing credentials were removed.
- **Extra missing on the auth commands:** the install-hint path is specified only for `create_agent` and `get_provider` (lines 76, 80, 122). The auth commands go strategy → `login.py`, which imports `openai_codex` inside the function. The criterion at line 190 ("any `openai-oauth` use exits with an error containing the exact install command") is therefore not shown to hold for `sq auth login` or `logout`.
- **Status with a login but no extra:** a user with `~/.codex/auth.json` from the Codex CLI and no extra hits the `account()` path on every `sq auth status`. The row at line 126 handles "timeout or SDK error"; an `ImportError` is neither. The design should say whether this case skips the account lookup silently or shows the hint, rather than logging a WARNING on every run.
- **Login runtime start failure:** the "subprocess fails to start" row is written for the turn path; say explicitly that it applies to login and logout too.

Add rows for these, and either a logout timeout key or a statement that `codex.account_timeout_s` covers logout.

findings.title: Version upper bound is both specified and declared undecided
findings.description: D1 gives the extra as `codex = ["openai-codex>=0.159.3,<1"]`, while the same sentence and line 231 say the upper bound "is not decided here … PM to say whether to cap". An implementer cannot tell which to write into `pyproject.toml`. An open Project Manager decision is also not a valid design step under the project rules. Pick one in the design: `<1` is defensible given the stated 0.x surface drift and the real-types drift test at line 200. Then delete the "PM to say" text.

findings.title: `--timeout` flag duplicates `codex.login_timeout_s`
findings.description: The slice plan entry asks for browser login and `--device-code`, not a per-invocation timeout. The config key already satisfies the no-magic-defaults rule, so `sq auth login --timeout` is a second control for the same value and can be cut along with its tests.

findings.title: Step 0 fallback check has no safe execution recipe
findings.description: Resolving the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback in this slice is justified by the no-silent-fallback principle, and both outcomes are specified. The procedure is the weak part: "unset `~/.codex/auth.json`" on the working machine logs the developer out, and the alternatives are "a throwaway `CODEX_HOME`-style location only if the runtime supports one" or "a machine without a login". State whether the runtime honors a relocated home directory, so the task breakdown gets a non-destructive step rather than a conditional.

findings.title: `sq model list` now loads every alias's provider
findings.description: D9 has `sq model list` call `ensure_provider_loaded` + `get_provider` for each alias's profile to test `isinstance(provider, ExtraRequirement)`. A listing command now depends on every provider module importing cleanly. The design should say what a row shows when a provider fails to load (for example, the row without a marker and a WARNING) so one broken provider does not abort the listing.

findings.title: Slice plan scope for 129 is fully covered
findings.description:
- **Part A:** port to `openai_codex`, bundled-then-PATH resolution, optional extra, effort via `ReasoningEffort` (closes #171), and per-turn usage are all present.
- **Part B:** install-hint error, doctor row, model-list marker and README are all present.
- **Part C:** browser and device-code login, logout, and email/plan in status are all present.

The exclusions (no squadron token store, no `login_api_key`, no streaming or approval work) match the plan's "squadron keeps no token store of its own". The smoke test in the plan appears as walkthrough step 6. Adding slice 931 as a dependency beyond the plan's `[128]` is correct, since effort and usage plumbing come from it.

findings.title: Auth capability respects the architecture's non-unified auth model
findings.description: The HLD's Authentication Patterns section says squadron does not unify authentication and each provider's credential resolution is self-contained. `InteractiveLogin` is an optional, separately checked Protocol implemented only by `OAuthFileStrategy`, delegating to the Codex runtime with no squadron-side credential storage. D3's choice of a separate Protocol over new `AuthStrategy` methods satisfies the plan's "capability on the strategy, not a profile-name check" and slice 128's ban on string dispatch.

findings.title: Dependency direction and layer boundaries are correct
findings.description:
- The CLI depends on provider-layer Protocols (`InteractiveLogin`, `ExtraRequirement`), never on `providers/codex` or SDK types.
- SDK types are confined to `agent.py` and `login.py`, with function-local imports so the module graph loads without the extra.
- The `notify` callback keeps Rich out of the provider layer.
- Doctor, agent and provider share one `CodexRuntime` resolver and one install-hint string.

findings.title: Codex turn failure modes are enumerated and observable
findings.description: Hang, timeout, mid-turn transport close, start failure, rate limiting, auth rejection, failed or interrupted turns, and empty responses each have an explicit behavior and a required test (line 199). D8's removal of `final_response or ""` closes a silent-fallback path.

findings.title: No architecture NFR applies; startup cost is addressed
findings.description: Neither the slice plan nor the HLD sets a latency or throughput target for provider turns or auth commands. The slice states where runtime spawn cost is paid (once per agent, never in doctor, model list or `create_agent`) and bounds the hang cases with config-level timeouts.
